title: Counit normalization of the short exact sequence cohomology tail
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian]. Suppose $\mathcal A$ has enough projectives: every object is a quotient of an object $P$ such that maps from $P$ lift across epimorphisms. Let $V:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive and right exact, meaning that it preserves cokernels and finite direct sums. Write $K(\mathcal A)$ and $K(\mathcal B)$ for the homotopy categories of integer cochain complexes and $Q_{\mathcal A},Q_{\mathcal B}$ for their localizations at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume the total left derived functor $LV:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ of the termwise functor $Q_{\mathcal B}K(V)$ is defined at every object in the essentially-constant denominator-diagram sense [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], with canonical natural comparison $\varepsilon_C:LV(Q_{\mathcal A}C)\to Q_{\mathcal B}V(C)$. Write $M[0]$ for the complex concentrated in degree zero. Put $T^q(N)=H^q(LV(Q_{\mathcal A}(N[0])))$ for $q\in\mathbf Z$, with maps $T^q(f)=H^q(LV(Q_{\mathcal A}(f[0])))$. Fix a short exact sequence $0\to M'\xrightarrow{i}M\xrightarrow{p}M''\to0$ and a distinguished triangle
$$LV(Q_{\mathcal A}(M'[0]))\xrightarrow{LV(Q_{\mathcal A}(i[0]))}LV(Q_{\mathcal A}(M[0]))\xrightarrow{LV(Q_{\mathcal A}(p[0]))}LV(Q_{\mathcal A}(M''[0]))\xrightarrow{w}LV(Q_{\mathcal A}(M'[0]))[1].$$
Then its connecting maps $\partial^q:T^q(M'')\to T^{q+1}(M')$ give an exact sequence
$$\cdots\to T^{q-1}(M'')\xrightarrow{\partial^{q-1}}T^q(M')\xrightarrow{T^q(i)}T^q(M)\xrightarrow{T^q(p)}T^q(M'')\xrightarrow{\partial^q}T^{q+1}(M')\to\cdots.$$
The maps $c_N=H^0(\varepsilon_{N[0]}):T^0(N)\to V(N)$, using the canonical identification $H^0(Q_{\mathcal B}(V(N)[0]))\cong V(N)$, are isomorphisms satisfying $c_{N_2}\circ T^0(f)=V(f)\circ c_{N_1}$ for every $f:N_1\to N_2$. All $T^q(N)$ vanish for $q>0$, and the normalized tail is exactly
$$T^{-1}(M'')\xrightarrow{c_{M'}\circ\partial^{-1}}V(M')\xrightarrow{V(i)}V(M)\xrightarrow{V(p)}V(M'')\to0.$$
In particular the arrows in this exact tail are the specified images under $V$, without any acyclicity assumption.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] in the abelian category $\mathcal B$ to the distinguished triangle stipulated in the statement. Set $X=LV(Q_{\mathcal A}(M'[0]))$, $Y=LV(Q_{\mathcal A}(M[0]))$, and $Z=LV(Q_{\mathcal A}(M''[0]))$. Its first two arrows are the specified images of $i[0]$ and $p[0]$, so their cohomology maps are exactly $T^q(i)$ and $T^q(p)$. Its connecting morphism, obtained from $H^q(w)$ and the cohomology identification for $[1]$, is $\partial^q$. The cited exact sequence, for all integer degrees, is therefore the asserted long exact sequence.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-left-derived-object-cohomology] to $V$ and each object $N$ of $\mathcal A$. Its hypotheses are precisely the given abelian categories, enough projectives, additivity, right exactness, and existence of the total left derived functor in the essentially-constant sense. It gives $T^q(N)=0$ for $q>0$ and identifies the actual $H^0(\varepsilon_{N[0]})$, not just some isomorphism, as an isomorphism $c_N:T^0(N)\to V(N)$. It also gives $c_{N_2}T^0(f)=V(f)c_{N_1}$ for every $f:N_1\to N_2$. In particular $T^1(M')=0$.

source.place: Duals of Tags 05TC (lemma-negative-vanishing) and 05TD (lemma-left-exact-higher-derived); Tag 05T5 (lemma-irrelevant), clauses (3),(4).

proof.text: The degree-zero segment of step 1 ends $T^{-1}(M'')\xrightarrow{\partial^{-1}}T^0(M')\xrightarrow{T^0(i)}T^0(M)\xrightarrow{T^0(p)}T^0(M'')\to0$ by step 2. Replace its three degree-zero objects by $V(M'),V(M),V(M'')$ through their $c$ isomorphisms. The resulting arrows are $c_{M'}\partial^{-1}$, $c_M T^0(i)c_{M'}^{-1}=V(i)$ and $c_{M''}T^0(p)c_M^{-1}=V(p)$, the two equalities being step 2 with $f=i,p$. This sequence is exact: composing with an isomorphism leaves an image subobject unchanged at its source side and carries it isomorphically at its target side, and the same universal-property calculation applies to kernels. Thus each image-kernel equality of step 1 is carried to the corresponding equality for these arrows; at the last object its kernel towards zero is the whole object. This is precisely the stated normalized exact tail, with no acyclicity hypothesis.
